en.html:
Please observe the peaceful village situation, because several dozen armed soldiers had arrived to improve it.

There was one open field in front. In this field the soldiers stood in matching military dress, same formation, rifles in hand and army swords also provided. For distance they had bullet. For closeness they had blade. Thus every geographical possibility had been considered.

Their fighting spirit was extremely present. Their voices were extremely absent. Not one man spoke. The setting sun had gone red behind them, laying the same colour over uniform and steel and making an already sinister gathering look fully confirmed.

At the front stood warriors in thick iron armour with very long swords. Behind them were several dozen ordinary soldiers. But do not count wrongly. One armoured fellow may have more fighting power than the whole quantity behind him. Mathematics will object, naturally. Mathematics has not seen his sword.

Then the foremost warrior shouted toward the village. Was he commander? Arre, listen only to the manner. A subordinate may be arrogant for himself. This man was arrogant for the entire unit. His rank came out of his mouth before the message.

He stepped out before the soldiers.

An armoured warrior, just like the men threatening the village. Only, look at the condition. Their armour had been maintained: plates secure, mechanisms ready, full fighting order. His damage had been left as it was. Whatever wore down was permitted to keep wearing.

Same kind of warrior. One with an army behind him; one with whatever parts were still managing.

He went to take another step. A small hand caught his.

The little girl said nothing. She only held on. Bas, don't go. Her whole request was in those fingers.

He looked down at her. Still without speaking, he stroked her head, then gently made her let go.

Her eyes filled. He turned away and walked on.

Several soldiers lifted their weapons to rush him. Their commander stopped them with one hand and came forward alone.

fallen wanderer"...What are you planning, Saginuma?"
unit commander"Showing respect to my old commanding officer. Major Kakei. Former Major, of course. Respect does not mean we neglect the correction."
fallen wanderer"You will spare the village. Zubaan pakki?"
unit commander"Hand you over, and the village answers for no crime. Exactly what I said."
fallen wanderer"Good. And you mean to fight me yourself? Itni badi baraat behind you, and now you want to come alone?"
unit commander"For one neck? Why should I inconvenience the whole army?"
fallen wanderer"..."
unit commander"Never defeated in single combat—that was your pride, na? You cannot carry it to hell. Leave it here. A traitor to Rokuhara is not entitled to honourable hand luggage."
fallen wanderer"...Achchha."
unit commander"Your wing-cloak is torn past twin-wheel mounting. We fight on the ground. I am not defeating half a man and spending the evening defending the fraction."
fallen wanderer"Wah, Saginuma. Yesterday the nose was running. Today the mouth has taken over. "Fine. Serve this feast you are promising. Your head will make a good souvenir for the journey."
unit commander"My head stays here, Kakei. Your wrinkled neck, however—tonight the drink will go down beautifully."

Both attacks were decided. Neither man moved.

Because both had also prepared the answer, and neither believed the other had come here without doing his homework.

Saginuma thrusts: Kakei twists aside, then cuts him down before he can recover.

Kakei cuts: Saginuma steps back, lets the sword pass, springs forward and puts the point through him.

Attack: certain death. Counterattack: also certain death. Itni preparation, and now nobody can start.

So they stood within killing distance, holding the stance, watching every smallest movement. The contest had become stamina and concentration. Imagine crossing a ravine on one rope and finding another man coming from the opposite side. Both of you have brought scissors.

Sooner or later one body would give. One guard would open. If the other man had strength left, he would take that opening and the victory with it.

Commander Saginuma. Fallen warrior Kakei.

Which man would do which part? Abhi that much remained undecided.

　しかし両者とも、不動にて時を送る。

　それは両者とも、攻め手に併せて受け手を用意して
おり、そしてどちらも、対敵にその備えがあることを
疑っていなかったからである。

　六波羅の将、鷺沼が突き出せば――
　垣見は僅かに身を捻るのみでその鋭鋒を<ruby>躱<rt>かわ</rt></ruby>し、鷺沼
が姿勢を立て直す前に斬り下ろして、勝負を決するで
あろう。

　落人、垣見が先に斬り掛かれば――
　鷺沼は一歩退いて剣撃を外し、すぐさま跳ね戻って
宿敵を刺し殺すであろう。

　攻め手が必殺なら受け手もまた必殺。
　互いに対敵の手の内を読み切り、<ruby>故<rt>ゆえ</rt></ruby>に動けず、戦況
は膠着する。

　かかる情勢、勝負は<ruby>即<rt>すなわ</rt></ruby>ち、体力気力の削り合い。

　垣見と鷺沼、対峙する二者は今、敵を一足一刀にて
仕留め得る体勢と敵の微細な変化をも見逃さぬ集中力、
その二つを維持しながら向き合っている。
　なればこその膠着。

　これが両者の心身に多大な負担を掛ける事は論ずる
までもない。
　渓谷を綱渡りするにも等しい過酷さである。

　やがては一方が力尽き、構を崩す。
　その時もう一方が余力を残していたならば、即座に
その崩れを狙って攻め掛かり、勝利者となるであろう。

　軍将、鷺沼。
　落人、垣見。
　
　いずれがいずれの役を負うか。

Age began putting in its small, dirty work.

Saginuma was in his middle years, strength still with him. Kakei was only somewhat older. Old age had not arrived, but it knew the address. The difference in stamina was small. Haan, small. A throat does not need a very large opening either.

The deadlock favoured Saginuma. Each moment cost Kakei more. Eventually his guard would give, and the sword would come through. To avoid that, he had to attack first, put everything into it, and kill Saginuma.

Simple advice. Useless advice. This was the fellow who had left his own army standing behind him to fight alone. Now he would become careless? He watched his former commander, present rebel, without giving one grain of opening.

Kakei rushes. Saginuma stops him. The answer comes back. Kakei dies.

Go forward: death.
Stay here: death, with the travelling saved.

From outside, stillness. A lake without a ripple. Underneath, victory and defeat were already settling toward their owners. Only the bodies had yet to find out.

　鷺沼が壮年の頃であるのに対して、垣見はそれより
やや年嵩、老境の迫りを肌に感じる年齢である。
　体力差は、大きくはないが、確かに存在する。

　鷺沼が優勢であった。
　膠着は若さを残す者に利する。

　垣見はやがて崩れ、敵刃に首を委ねるであろう。
　その運命を望まぬなら、乾坤一擲、自ら攻め出して

の油断もなく、昔の上官であり今の叛徒である対手を
見据えているのだ。

　破れかぶれの猪突など容易く防ぎ、完璧な返し技で
勝ってのけるだろう。

　落人垣見の進退は窮まった。

　進めば、死。
　進まずとも、死。

　傍目には、湖面のように移ろわぬ情景。
　されど水面の下、勝利と敗北、栄誉と破滅の天秤は
傾きを定めつつある。

The sword did not come down. It changed course and settled beside Kakei's left flank.

An upward cut.

Show him the downward blow, make him retreat, then follow with the real one. His timing broken, his attention above, and the blade coming from below—under the arm or into the groin, where the armour's protection thinned. Before Saginuma could understand the mistake and spring back, it could be finished.

One man surprised; one man expecting it. Who moves first? Arre, guess.

Earlier, Saginuma would have seen through this. Abhi, though, Kakei really was cornered. The desperation was genuine. Only the attack was lying.

The idea came in a flash. His end might be decided, but this one fight—nahin, this one he could still win.

In that instant, the whole situation turned.

　使い手の左脇へ、新たに構えられる。

　斬り上げの剣形。

　斬り下ろしの幻で敵を退かせ、
　その隙を追い、本命の一刀を繰り出す。

Machetes, hoes, hand axes. Jo mila, whatever the sheds could give. Villagers hid with them behind walls and struck at soldiers who passed carelessly.

A hunter brought out an old long gun. He knew how to move, how to wait, when to fire. One soldier at a time. No wasted chance.

Each startled face falling made something inside him happier, and less sane. Aur. More. You killed this many; I will kill this many. His anger was still trying to balance the count.

It would not get the chance. Something that had no reason to fear him had already chosen him.

Years of hunting kept him out of the soldiers' sight. Every hiding place, every movement—on the ground, nobody could see him.

An ordinary man could not do this. Haan, correct. The flying fellow inside the armour was not an ordinary man. The armour gave him strength outside the human limit. Whatever name you preferred, the practical difficulty was that you were facing a demon.

Until then, the others had watched the foot soldiers work. Once the first rider descended, the rest followed. Beside their violence, the soldiers' cruelty was an early-spring breeze.

The man did not look trained, yet every shot found its target. Four bullets flew toward four armoured warriors.

A miracle, and an entirely useless one.

One warrior tilted his head and let the bullet pass. One cut his bullet aside. One caught his in a bare hand. The fourth fellow did nothing.

The round struck his abdomen, left no mark, and fell. Even the bullet appeared to understand it had entered the wrong profession.

All four handled supersonic bullets the way a man handles flies.

He threw himself into the village's only truck and rolled into the driver's seat. He stamped the accelerator as though sufficient pressure would manufacture a road beneath it.

For one instant he may have imagined the truck moving, carrying him away from the demons. Perhaps he became generous and imagined his companions climbing into the back. Terror had given him transport, route and passengers without moving one wheel.

The truck would never move.

He was at least spared the time required to discover this.

One man ran.

He hit his companions, pushed them aside, stepped over fallen family. Not malice. Bas, fear. The body had one instruction left and was obeying it with everything.

Through the crowd. There, the road. The next village. Keep running and he could reach it. Reach it and be saved.

Don't look back. Bhaag. Run, keep running, sooner or later—

Thirty seconds passed before he understood that he had not moved one step.

An armoured warrior was above him, swimming through the sky, one hand holding his collar. All this time his legs had been running through empty air.

en.html:
The little girl, her ankle cut, kept trying to understand.

Kyun? Why?

Yesterday was an ordinary day. Papa went into the mountains to cut timber. Ma looked after the house. She played with her friends, helped a little at home. The same things, day after day. Nothing changed.

Then all of it broke. Ekdum. Just like that.

Why had the army come? Why her village? What was the reason?

Her teacher had explained it: do something bad, and it comes back to you. Hurt someone, and one day you will be hurt.

Achchha, but whom had she hurt? Papa? Ma? All these people who were dead? Her friends lying beside her with their legs cut?

Was it wrong to give Kakei somewhere to sleep? To feed him? He had been kind. Every grown-up said what a good samurai he was.

Toh phir? What else had they done? What was she not understanding?

足首を切られた童女は思う。
　
　――なぜだろう。

　昨日までは村で普通に暮らしていた。

　父は山に入って木を切り出す林業に携わり、
　母は家の一切を取り仕切り、
　自分は友達と遊びつつ、時折母の手伝いをした。

　繰り返しの日々。
　何も変わらない毎日。

　それが唐突に壊される……
　どんな理由で、そんなことが起こるのだろう。

　あの軍隊というものがやって来て、村を滅茶滅茶に
してしまったのは、なんでだろう。

　学校の先生は教えてくれた。
　悪いことをすると自分に返ってくるのです。誰かに

と。

足首を切られた童女は思う。

　昨日までは村で普通に暮らしていた。

　父は山に入って木を切り出す林業に携わり、
　母は家の一切を取り仕切り、

　繰り返しの日々。
　何も変わらない毎日。

　あの軍隊というものがやって来て、村を滅茶滅茶に

　学校の先生は教えてくれた。

と。

If they were being punished for hurting someone, then these soldiers—what about them?

The same thing had to come back to them. It had to, na? Otherwise how did the lesson work?

But who would do it?

The army could destroy the village. Who could destroy the army? Who was strong enough to punish the men inside this armour?

Shayad nobody.

Then it ended here. They received all the punishment without even knowing their crime. The men doing this, doing it right in front of her, would receive nothing. Because nobody could make them.

Nahin. That was wrong. That could not be how it worked.

The girl who could no longer stand cried out inside herself, amid breaking things and screams.

Someone. Koi toh.

I won't ask you to save us. Just don't let it end with us. Please.

Give it to them too. This hurt. This sorrow. Make what they have done come back to them.

Bhagwan, please.

Everything had been taken from her. Grief and pure anger were all she had for the prayer.

This is wrong. Please make it right.

何か酷いことをしたから、こんな目にあうのか。
　
　なら、<ruby>これ<rt>・・</rt></ruby>をした連中は？

　この連中も、いずれ同じ目にあうのだろうか。
　そうでなくては、おかしい。筋道が通らない。

　でも、誰が？

　村は軍隊の圧倒的な力で滅茶滅茶にされた。
　けど、軍隊は誰が滅茶滅茶にしてくれるのだろう。

　誰にそんなことができるのだろう。
　誰がこの、鎧の人々を罰せられるのだろう。

　誰もいないのではないか。

　誰もいないのなら。
　罰の連鎖はここで終わり。

　どんな悪いことをしたのかもわからない自分達だけ
が罰を受けて、確かに酷いことをしたこの連中は何の
報いも受けない。
　だって、誰も彼らを罰することができないのだから。

　おかしい。
　おかしいよ。

　破壊と悲鳴の楽奏の中、立てない童女は叫ぶ。
　
　――こんなの、おかしいよ。

　誰か。誰か。
　助けてとは言いません。
　お願い。<ruby>わたしたちで終わらせないで<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　あいつらにも罰を。
　悪いことをした報いを。
　同じ苦痛と悲しみを。

　誰か、与えてください。
　神様。
　お願いです。

　童女は祈る。
　奪われた者の嘆き、純粋な怒りを胸に。

　お願いします。
　こんなことは間違っているのだから。
　どうか、正しくしてください。

A song could be heard.

The girl understood. All this time, she had understood wrongly.

Achchha. Is that it, Bhagwan?

She listened. The song was singing life.

Good things, bad things—living wasn't about those? That wasn't the meaning?

The song answered. Where life lives, no crime. No punishment. Life only has to be life, purely, with nothing else put on top. That was the right way.

The girl sang. She sang life. She sang joy.

Oh. We only had to live with our whole hearts. Bas, to be living things. Only that one thing to pursue.

Simply live. As a creature, as life. Honest. Pure—

en.html:
Two meteors crossed the sky, turned, crossed again.

The red star came like a starving wolf. The silver one moved lightly as a doe.

A roar hit the night. Laughter went through it.

The warrior in red swung his sword with grief in the sound. Silver received it as softly as an embrace and turned it aside. He brought anger, shame, frustration, sorrow—sab kuch. She met it with joy, comfort, acceptance, delight.

Act Four.

Another duel, then? Like the first act?

Nahin. Not this.

This was communion. Play.

One graceless man with all his fury, and one elegant princess who would not even treat that fury as a proper difficulty.

――二条の流星は天を駆け巡り交差しまた巡る。

　赤の星は餓狼めいて獰猛に。
　銀の星は雌鹿めいて軽やかに。

　咆哮が夜空を叩く。
　笑声が夜空を渡る。

　赤色の武人は慟哭の響きで太刀を繰り出し、
　銀色の武人は抱擁の柔らかさでそれを流す。

　怒りを、慙愧を、無念を、悲嘆を、
　喜びが、慰撫が、許容が、愉悦が迎える。

　第四幕――
　この夜最後の一幕は、最初の幕に<ruby>倣<rt>なら</rt></ruby>っての決闘か。

　否。
　そうでは、ない。

　これは<ruby>交情<rt>まじわり</rt></ruby>。

　戯れであった。
　無粋な男と、彼をあしらう高雅な姫の。

en.html:
The silver fairy climbed higher. Higher still. The crimson demon fell behind, as though hell itself were calling him back.

Silver reached the height of heaven.

With the moon behind her like a throne, she looked down at the red demon still struggling upward. Abhi bhi, even now, he was trying.

Behind the helmet, smiling lips sang one line.
